constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000
1 <= name.length() <= 50
Name contains only alphabets.
Initial ID is 1001.
explanation: nextId is static, so it is shared among all employee objects. For every object: (1) Assign nextId to id, (2) Increment nextId, (3) Increment employee count.

title: Static Configuration Manager
statement: Use a static block to initialize default application configuration: Environment = Development, MaxUsers = 100. Then update the configuration using a static method.
explanation: The static block provides default configuration. The static update() method modifies the shared class-level values.

title: Static Employee Salary Statistics
statement: Create an Employee class where: every employee stores an individual salary, a static variable stores total salary, a static variable stores employee count, and a static method returns average salary.
explanation: Every object updates the shared count and totalSalary. average = totalSalary / count.

title: Employee Salary Using Runtime Polymorphism
statement: Create a base Employee class. Developer gets 10% bonus. Manager gets 20% bonus. Override calculateSalary().
constraints:
Salary: 0-10^9
Type is either Developer or Manager.
explanation: The reference variable is of type Employee, but the actual object is Developer. Therefore Java invokes the overridden calculateSalary() method at runtime.

title: Shape Area Using Abstraction
statement: Create an abstract class Shape. Implement Circle, Rectangle, and Triangle. Each class must implement area().
constraints:
Dimensions are positive.
0 < radius, length, width, base, height <= 10^6
explanation: Shape defines what every shape must provide, but does not specify how the area is calculated. Each subclass provides its own implementation.

title: Payment System Using Interface
statement: Create a Payment interface and implement UPI, CreditCard, and NetBanking.
explanation: The interface defines a common pay() contract. Each implementation decides how the payment is performed.

title: Vehicle Hierarchy
statement: Create a base class Vehicle and subclasses: Car (18 km/l), Bike (45 km/l), Truck (8 km/l). Override calculateMileage().
constraints: Type is one of the three specified types.
explanation: The same reference type Vehicle can point to different subclass objects.

title: Notification System
statement: Create a Notification interface with implementations: Email, SMS, Push.
explanation: The interface provides abstraction and allows different notification classes to follow the same contract.
timeComplexity: O(L) where L is message length

title: Abstract Employee Bonus
statement: Create an abstract Employee class. Developer bonus = 15%. Manager bonus = 25%.
explanation: Because calculateBonus() is abstract, each subclass must implement its own bonus logic.

title: Multiple Interfaces
statement: Create two interfaces: Printable, Scannable. Create a Printer class that implements both.
explanation: Java does not support multiple inheritance through classes, but a class can implement multiple interfaces.

title: Banking Polymorphism
statement: Create: Account, SavingsAccount, CurrentAccount. Savings account interest = 6%. Current account interest = 2%.
explanation: The method invoked depends on the actual object created, demonstrating runtime polymorphism.

title: Abstract Notification Validation
statement: Create an abstract Notification class with validate() and send(). Email is valid if it contains '@'. SMS is valid if its length is exactly 10.
constraints:
Message length: 1-100
SMS contains digits.
Email contains at least one '@'.
explanation: The base class defines the general notification behavior. Each subclass provides its own validation rule.

title: E-Commerce Product Hierarchy
statement: Create an abstract Product class. Electronics -> 18% tax. Clothing -> 10% discount. Grocery -> 5% tax. Calculate the final price.
explanation: Each subclass applies its own pricing rule through method overriding.

title: First Non-Repeating Character
statement: Find the first character that occurs exactly once.
constraints:
1 <= length <= 100000
String contains lowercase English letters.
explanation: Frequencies: s -> 3, w -> 1, i -> 1. The first character having frequency 1 is w.

title: Remove Duplicate Characters
statement: Remove duplicate characters while preserving their first occurrence.
explanation: Characters are added to the result only the first time they are encountered.

title: Longest Word in a Sentence
statement: Find the longest word in a sentence. If two words have the same length, return the first one.
constraints:
1 <= sentence.length() <= 100000
Words are separated by spaces.
explanation: The word lengths are: Java -> 4, programming -> 11, language -> 7. Therefore programming is longest.

title: String Compression
statement: Compress consecutive characters. Example: aaabbccccd becomes a3b2c4d1.
constraints:
1 <= length <= 100000
String contains lowercase English letters.
explanation: Count consecutive occurrences of each character and append both the character and its count using StringBuilder.

title: Anagram Without Sorting
statement: Determine whether two strings are anagrams without sorting them.
constraints:
1 <= length <= 100000
Strings contain lowercase English letters.
explanation: Both strings contain exactly the same frequency of every character.

title: Palindrome Ignoring Spaces and Case
sampleInput: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
statement: Determine whether a sentence is a palindrome after ignoring spaces, case, and special characters.
explanation: After removing non-alphanumeric characters and converting to lowercase: amanaplanacanalpanama. It reads the same forward and backward.

title: Reverse Words
statement: Reverse the order of words without reversing individual characters.
explanation: The words are stored and processed from the last word to the first.

title: String Rotation
statement: Determine whether string B is a rotation of string A.
constraints:
1 <= length <= 100000
Both strings contain lowercase letters.
explanation: If B is a rotation of A, then B must be present inside A + A. For example, ABCDABCD contains CDAB.
timeComplexity: O(N) average for the practical string-search approach

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
statement: Find the length of the longest substring containing no repeated characters.
explanation: The longest substrings without repetition include abc, which has length 3. A sliding-window approach maintains the current unique substring.

title: Compare Strings Without equals()
statement: Implement your own string comparison method without using equals() or compareTo(). Return true only when both strings are exactly identical.
explanation: First compare lengths. If they are equal, compare every corresponding character.

title: Matrix Multiplication
statement: Multiply two matrices. Matrix multiplication is possible only if columns of A = rows of B.
explanation: Each result cell is calculated as result[i][j] = sum of a[i][k] x b[k][j].

title: Spiral Matrix Traversal
statement: Print the elements of a matrix in spiral order.
explanation: Maintain four boundaries: top, bottom, left, right. Process one outer layer at a time.

title: Rotate Matrix 90 Degrees
statement: Rotate a square matrix by 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
explanation: A clockwise rotation can be achieved using two operations: (1) Transpose the matrix, (2) Reverse every row.

title: Row With Maximum Sum
statement: Find the row having the maximum sum. Return the row number using 1-based indexing.
explanation: Row sums: Row 1 -> 6, Row 2 -> 11, Row 3 -> 6. Therefore row 2 is selected.

title: Saddle Point in Matrix
statement: Find an element that is minimum in its row and maximum in its column. Such an element is called a saddle point.
explanation: Note: the naive 1-9 ascending matrix example is a common ambiguity trap for this definition -- its row-minimums are not column-maximums, so it yields no saddle point. The corrected sample below is consistent with the stated definition. Here 3 is the minimum in its row (3, 4, 5) and, checking its column (3, 2, 1), it is also the maximum in that column.

title: Diagonal Difference
statement: Calculate the absolute difference between the primary and secondary diagonal sums of a square matrix.
explanation: Primary diagonal: 1 + 5 + 9 = 15. Secondary diagonal: 3 + 5 + 7 = 15. Difference: |15 - 15| = 0.

title: Encapsulated Bank Account
statement: Create a BankAccount class where balance is private. Implement deposit(), withdraw(), getBalance(). Withdrawal should fail when the amount is greater than the available balance.
explanation: balance cannot be directly modified outside the class because it is private. The class controls access through public methods.

title: Utility Class for Array Operations
statement: Create a utility class similar to one that could be placed inside a package such as utilities. Implement static methods: maximum(), minimum(), average().
explanation: A utility class contains reusable static methods, so an object does not need to be created.

title: Encapsulated Student Result
statement: Create a Student class where marks are private. Implement setMarks(), getMarks(), calculateAverage(), calculateGrade(). Grade rules: >=90 A, >=75 B, >=60 C, >=50 D, otherwise F.
explanation: The marks array is private, so outside code cannot directly modify it. The public methods provide controlled access. Average = (80+90+70)/3 = 80, so grade is B.

title: Weird Algorithm
statement:
Consider an algorithm that takes as input a positive integer n. If n is even, the algorithm divides it by two, and if n is odd, the algorithm multiplies it by three and adds one. The algorithm repeats this, until n is one.

Your task is to simulate the execution of the algorithm for a given value of n.
constraints:
1 <= n <= 10^6
Note: Intermediate values can exceed 32-bit signed integer limits; use 64-bit integers (long in Java / long long in C++).
explanation: Starting from n, repeatedly print n and update n = (n % 2 == 0) ? n / 2 : 3 * n + 1 until n == 1. Use a 64-bit integer type to avoid overflow.

title: Missing Number
statement: You are given all numbers between 1, 2, ..., n except one. Your task is to find the missing number.
explanation: The sum of numbers from 1 to n is n*(n+1)/2. Subtract the sum of the given n-1 numbers from n*(n+1)/2 (using 64-bit long) to obtain the missing number.

title: Repetitions
statement: You are given a DNA sequence: a string consisting of characters A, C, G, and T. Your task is to find the longest repetition in the sequence. This is a maximum-length substring containing only one type of character.
explanation: Maintain the current run length cur and maximum run length best. Whenever s[i] == s[i-1], increment cur; otherwise reset cur = 1.

title: Increasing Array
statement:
You are given an array of n integers. You want to modify the array so that it is increasing, i.e., every element is at least as large as the previous element.

On each move, you may increase the value of any element by one. What is the minimum number of moves required?
explanation: Track the maximum element seen so far (mx). If the current element x < mx, we must increment it by (mx - x) moves, and its new value becomes mx.

title: Permutations
statement:
A permutation of integers 1, 2, ..., n is called beautiful if there are no adjacent elements whose difference is 1.

Given n, construct a beautiful permutation by printing all even integers in increasing order followed by all odd integers in increasing order, or print "NO SOLUTION" if no such permutation exists.
explanation: For n = 1, the answer is "1". For n = 2 and n = 3, no valid arrangement exists ("NO SOLUTION"). For n >= 4, printing all even numbers (2, 4, 6, ...) followed by all odd numbers (1, 3, 5, ...) guarantees adjacent differences are at least 2.

title: Number Spiral
statement:
A number spiral is an infinite grid whose upper-left square has number 1. Here are the first five layers of the spiral:

1  2  9 10 25
4  3  8 11 24
5  6  7 12 23
16 15 14 13 22
17 18 19 20 21

Your task is to find the number in row y and column x.
explanation: Let z = max(y, x). The L-shaped layer z contains numbers from (z-1)^2 + 1 to z^2. Depending on whether z is even or odd, the numbers increase clockwise or counter-clockwise.

title: Two Knights
statement: Your task is to count for k = 1, 2, ..., n the number of ways two knights can be placed on a k x k chessboard so that they do not attack each other.
explanation: Total ways to place two identical knights on k^2 squares is k^2 * (k^2 - 1) / 2. Every 2x3 or 3x2 subgrid contains 2 attacking pairs. There are (k-1)(k-2) subgrids of each orientation, so subtract 4 * (k-1) * (k-2).

title: Two Sets
statement: Your task is to divide the numbers 1, 2, ..., n into two sets of equal sum. Print "NO" if it is impossible, otherwise print "YES" followed by the number of elements and elements of the first set (picked greedily from n down to 1), and then the second set in decreasing order.
explanation: The sum S = n(n+1)/2 is even iff n % 4 == 0 or n % 4 == 3. When S is even, greedily iterate from n down to 1: if the current number <= remaining target sum S/2, place it in Set 1 and subtract from target; otherwise place it in Set 2.

title: Bit Strings
statement:
Your task is to calculate the number of bit strings of length n.
For example, if n = 3, the correct answer is 8, because the possible bit strings are 000, 001, 010, 011, 100, 101, 110, and 111.

Print the result modulo 10^9 + 7.
explanation: Each of the n positions has 2 choices (0 or 1), yielding 2^n modulo 1000000007.

title: Trailing Zeros
statement:
Your task is to calculate the number of trailing zeros in the factorial n!.
For example, 20! = 2432902008176640000 and it has 4 trailing zeros.
explanation: Trailing zeros are produced by factors of 10 = 2 * 5. Since factors of 2 are always more plentiful than 5, count the powers of 5 dividing n!: floor(n/5) + floor(n/25) + floor(n/125) + ...

title: Coin Piles
statement:
You have two coin piles containing a and b coins. On each move, you can either remove one coin from the left pile and two coins from the right pile, or two coins from the left pile and one coin from the right pile.

Your task is to efficiently find out if you can empty both the piles.
explanation: Each move removes 3 coins in total, so (a + b) must be divisible by 3. Furthermore, the larger pile cannot have more than twice the coins of the smaller pile: max(a, b) <= 2 * min(a, b).

title: Palindrome Reorder
statement: Given a string of uppercase letters A-Z, your task is to reorder its letters in such a way that it becomes the lexicographically smallest palindrome (or print "NO SOLUTION" if impossible).
explanation: Count frequencies of A-Z. At most one character can have an odd count. Construct the left half using count[c]/2 copies of each letter from A to Z, place the odd character (if any) in the middle, and append the reversed left half.

title: Gray Code
statement:
A Gray code is a list of all 2^n bit strings of length n, where any two successive strings differ in exactly one bit (i.e., their Hamming distance is one).

Generate the standard binary reflected Gray code where the i-th string (0 <= i < 2^n) is the n-bit binary representation of i ^ (i >> 1).
explanation: The standard Gray code for integer i is given by g(i) = i ^ (i >> 1). Format each value as an n-bit binary string padded with leading zeros.

title: Tower of Hanoi
statement:
The Tower of Hanoi game consists of three stacks (left = 1, middle = 2, right = 3) and n round disks of different sizes. Initially, the left stack has all the disks, in increasing order of size from top to bottom.

The goal is to move all the disks to the right stack using the middle stack. First print the minimum number of moves, then print each move "a b".
explanation: Moving n disks from stack A to stack C using auxiliary stack B requires: (1) move n-1 disks from A to B, (2) move disk n from A to C, (3) move n-1 disks from B to C. Total moves: 2^n - 1.

title: Apple Division
statement: There are n apples with known weights. Your task is to divide the apples into two groups so that the difference between the weights of the groups is minimal.
explanation: Since n <= 20, there are only 2^n <= 1,048,576 subsets. Iterate over all bitmasks (or recursively branch on each apple) and minimize |totalSum - 2 * subsetSum|.

title: Distinct Numbers
statement: You are given a list of n integers, and your task is to calculate the number of distinct values in the list.
explanation: Sort the array and count adjacent elements that differ (arr[i] != arr[i-1]), or insert all elements into a HashSet.

title: Apartments
statement:
There are n applicants and m free apartments. Your task is to distribute the apartments so that as many applicants as possible will get an apartment.

Each applicant has a desired apartment size, and they will accept any apartment whose size is close enough to the desired size (within +-k).
explanation: Sort both applicant desires and apartment sizes. Use two pointers i and j: if |a[i] - b[j]| <= k, match them and advance both; if b[j] < a[i] - k, apartment j is too small so j++; otherwise i++.
timeComplexity: O(N log N + M log M)

title: Ferris Wheel
statement:
There are n children who want to go to a Ferris wheel, and your task is to find a gondola for each child.

Each gondola may have one or two children in it, and in addition, the total weight in a gondola may not exceed x. You know the weight of every child.

What is the minimum number of gondolas needed for the children?
explanation: Sort weights. Pair the heaviest remaining child (right pointer r) with the lightest remaining child (left pointer l) if p[l] + p[r] <= x; otherwise the heaviest child rides alone. Each step uses 1 gondola.

title: Restaurant Customers
statement:
You are given the arrival and leaving times of n customers in a restaurant.

What was the maximum number of customers in the restaurant at any time?
constraints:
1 <= n <= 2 * 10^5
1 <= a < b <= 10^9
All arrival and leaving times are distinct.
explanation: Convert each customer into two events: (+1 at arrival a) and (-1 at departure b). Sort events by timestamp and maintain the running sum and its maximum.

title: Movie Festival
concept: Greedy Interval Scheduling (Sort by End Time)
statement: In a movie festival n movies will be shown. You know the starting and ending time of each movie. What is the maximum number of movies you can watch entirely?
explanation: Classic interval scheduling: sort movies in ascending order of their ending time b. Greedily pick the next movie whose start time a >= lastEnd.

title: Sum of Two Values
statement:
You are given an array of n integers, and your task is to find two values (at distinct 1-based positions i < j) whose sum is x.

Print the two 1-based positions in increasing order (preferring the earliest second index j if multiple exist), or print "IMPOSSIBLE" if no solution exists.
explanation: Iterate j from 1 to n. Check if (x - a[j]) is already in our HashMap of seen values. If found at index i, print i and j and terminate.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum
statement: Given an array of n integers, your task is to find the maximum sum of values in a contiguous, non-empty subarray.
explanation: By Kadane's algorithm, the maximum subarray ending at index i is cur = max(a[i], cur + a[i]). Track the global maximum across all i.

title: Stick Lengths
statement:
There are n sticks with some lengths. Your task is to modify the sticks so that each stick has the same length.

You can either lengthen and shorten each stick. Both operations cost x where x is the difference between the new and original length.

What is the minimum total cost?
explanation: The sum of absolute deviations sum(|p_i - T|) is minimized when T is the median of the array (p[n/2] after sorting).

title: Missing Coin Sum
statement: You have n coins with positive integer values. What is the smallest sum you cannot create using a subset of the coins?
explanation: Sort the coins. Maintain the smallest unreachable value target = 1 (meaning all sums in [1, target-1] are achievable). If the next coin c <= target, we can extend our reachable range to [1, target + c - 1]; otherwise target cannot be formed.

title: Collecting Numbers
statement:
You are given an array that contains each number between 1 ... n exactly once. Your task is to collect the numbers from 1 to n in increasing order.

On each round, you go through the array from left to right and collect as many numbers as possible. How many rounds will it take?
explanation: Store the index pos[v] of each value v in 1..n. Start with 1 round. Whenever pos[v] < pos[v - 1], value v appears to the left of v - 1, so we must start a new round.

title: Towers
statement:
You are given n cubes in a certain order, and your task is to build towers using them. Whenever two cubes are one on top of the other, the upper cube must be strictly smaller than the lower cube.

You must process the cubes in the given order. What is the minimum possible number of towers?
explanation: Maintain a sorted list of the top cube sizes of all active towers. For each incoming cube x, binary search for the smallest tower top strictly greater than x (upper_bound). If found, replace that top with x; otherwise start a new tower.

title: Subarray Sums I
statement: Given an array of n positive integers, your task is to count the number of subarrays having sum x.
explanation: Maintain prefix sum frequencies in a HashMap (or use a two-pointer sliding window since all elements are positive). For each prefix sum P, add count[P - x] to the answer.

title: Dice Combinations
statement:
Your task is to count the number of ways to construct sum n by throwing a dice one or more times. Each throw produces an outcome between 1 and 6.

Print the number of ways modulo 10^9 + 7.
explanation: Let dp[s] be the number of ways to form sum s. Base case: dp[0] = 1. For each s from 1 to n, dp[s] = sum_{d=1..6, s-d >= 0} dp[s - d] (mod 10^9 + 7).

title: Minimizing Coins
statement:
Consider a money system consisting of n coins. Each coin has a positive integer value. Your task is to produce a sum of money x using the available coins in such a way that the number of coins is minimal.

Print one integer: the minimum number of coins, or -1 if it is not possible.
explanation: Initialize dp[0] = 0 and dp[1..x] = INF. For each coin c and sum s from c to x: dp[s] = min(dp[s], dp[s - c] + 1).

title: Coin Combinations I
statement:
Consider a money system consisting of n coins. Each coin has a positive integer value. Your task is to calculate the number of distinct ordered ways you can produce a money sum x using the available coins.

Print the number of ways modulo 10^9 + 7.
explanation: Because order matters, the outer loop iterates over sums s = 1..x and the inner loop iterates over coins c: dp[s] = (dp[s] + dp[s - c]) % MOD.

title: Coin Combinations II
statement:
Consider a money system consisting of n coins. Your task is to calculate the number of distinct unordered ways you can produce a money sum x using the available coins.

Print the number of ways modulo 10^9 + 7.
explanation: Because order does NOT matter, the outer loop iterates over each coin c and the inner loop iterates over sums s = c..x: dp[s] = (dp[s] + dp[s - c]) % MOD.

title: Removing Digits
statement:
You are given an integer n. On each step, you may subtract one of the digits from the number.

How many steps are required to make the number equal to 0?
explanation: At any number v > 0, subtracting its maximum decimal digit (or taking min over all digits d > 0 of dp[v - d] + 1) yields the minimum steps.

title: Grid Paths
statement:
Consider an n x n grid whose squares may have traps (*). It is not allowed to move to a square with a trap.

Your task is to calculate the number of paths from the upper-left square to the lower-right square. You can only move right or down. Print the answer modulo 10^9 + 7.
explanation: dp[r][c] = 0 if grid[r][c] == "*", else dp[r][c] = (dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1]) % MOD with base case dp[0][0] = 1 (if not a trap).

title: Book Shop
statement:
You are in a book shop which sells n different books. You know the price and number of pages of each book.

You have decided that the total price of your purchases will be at most x. What is the maximum number of pages you can buy? You can buy each book at most once.
explanation: Classic 0/1 Knapsack: maintain 1D array dp[0..x]. For each book i with price h and pages s, iterate budget w backwards from x down to h: dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w - h] + s).

title: Edit Distance
statement:
The edit distance between two strings is the minimum number of operations required to transform one string into the other.

The allowed operations are:
- Add one character to the string.
- Remove one character from the string.
- Replace one character in the string.

Calculate the edit distance between two given strings.
explanation: Let dp[i][j] be the edit distance between prefixes s1[0..i) and s2[0..j). If s1[i-1] == s2[j-1], dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]; else 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1]).

title: Increasing Subsequence
concept: O(N log N) Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS)
statement: You are given an array containing n integers. Your task is to determine the longest strictly increasing subsequence in the array, i.e., the longest subsequence where every element is larger than the previous one.
explanation: Maintain tails[k] = smallest tail of all increasing subsequences of length k+1. For each x, binary search (lower_bound) in tails and replace or append.

title: Money Sums
statement:
You have n coins with certain values. Your task is to find all money sums you can create using these coins.

First print the number of distinct positive sums, then print all possible sums in increasing order.
explanation: The maximum total sum is S <= 100,000. Use a boolean array reachable[0..S] with reachable[0] = true. For each coin c, iterate s from S down to c and set reachable[s] |= reachable[s - c].

title: Counting Rooms
concept: Grid Connected Components (BFS / DFS Flood Fill)
statement: You are given a map of a building, and your task is to count the number of its rooms. The size of the map is n x m squares, and each square is either floor (.) or wall (#). You can walk left, right, up, and down through the floor squares.
explanation: Iterate over every cell (r, c). Whenever an unvisited floor cell "." is found, increment the room counter and run BFS/DFS flood fill to mark all connected "." cells as visited.

title: Labyrinth (Shortest Path Distance)
statement:
You are given a map of a labyrinth of size n x m, and your task is to find the shortest path from start A to end B.

Print "YES" followed by the minimum number of steps on the next line if a path exists, or print "NO" if B is unreachable.
explanation: Run breadth-first search (BFS) starting from cell A. Since all edges have unit weight 1, the first time BFS reaches B gives the shortest path distance.

title: Building Roads
statement:
Byteland has n cities, and m roads between them. The goal is to construct new roads so that there is a route between any two cities.

Your task is to find the minimum number of new roads required. If C is the number of connected components, the answer is C - 1.
explanation: Use Disjoint Set Union (Union-Find) or DFS to count the number of connected components C. Connecting C components into a single connected graph requires exactly C - 1 edges.

title: Message Route
statement: Syrjälä's network has n computers and m connections. Your task is to find if Uolevi can send a message to Maija (from computer 1 to computer n), and if it is possible, what is the minimum number of computers on such a route (including 1 and n). Print "IMPOSSIBLE" if no route exists.
explanation: Run BFS from vertex 1. Track dist[u] (number of nodes on shortest path from 1 to u, with dist[1] = 1). Output dist[n] or "IMPOSSIBLE".

title: Shortest Routes I
statement:
There are n cities and m flight connections between them. Your task is to determine the length of the shortest route from Syrjälä (city 1) to every city 1, 2, ..., n.
All flight Connections are directed with positive edge weights.
explanation: Use Dijkstra's algorithm with a min-PriorityQueue storing (distance, vertex) pairs. Use 64-bit longs for distances.

title: Shortest Routes II
statement: There are n cities and m two-way roads between them. Your task is to process q queries where you have to determine the length of the shortest route between two given cities (or -1 if no route exists).
explanation: Run Floyd-Warshall in O(n^3): dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]) for intermediate k = 1..n. Handle multiple edges between the same pair by keeping the minimum weight.

title: Subordinates
statement: Given the structure of a company of n employees (employee 1 is the general director, and you are given the direct boss of each employee 2, 3, ..., n), calculate for each employee the total number of their subordinates (direct and indirect).
explanation: In a rooted tree at 1, the number of subordinates of node u is (subtreeSize[u] - 1). Process nodes in reverse topological order (or post-order DFS) accumulating child subtree sizes into their parent.

title: Tree Diameter
statement: You are given a tree consisting of n nodes. The diameter of a tree is the maximum distance between two nodes. Your task is to determine the diameter of the tree.
explanation: Run BFS from an arbitrary node (node 1) to find the farthest node X. Then run a second BFS starting from X; the maximum distance from X to any node is the diameter of the tree.

title: Static Range Sum Queries
statement: Given an array of n integers, your task is to process q queries of the form: what is the sum of values in range [a, b] (1-indexed)?
explanation: Precompute prefix sums pref[i] = pref[i-1] + x[i] in O(n) time. Each query [a, b] is answered in O(1) as pref[b] - pref[a-1].

title: Static Range Minimum Queries
statement: Given an array of n integers, your task is to process q queries of the form: what is the minimum value in range [a, b] (1-indexed)?
explanation: Build a Sparse Table st[k][i] = minimum in [i, i + 2^k - 1] in O(n log n) time. Answer each query [a, b] in O(1) using k = floor(log2(b - a + 1)).

title: Dynamic Range Sum Queries
concept: Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree) / Segment Tree
statement:
Given an array of n integers, your task is to process q queries of the following types:
1. update the value at position k to u
2. what is the sum of values in range [a, b]?
explanation: Maintain a Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree) supporting point add in O(log n) and prefix sum in O(log n).

title: Range Xor Queries
statement: Given an array of n integers, your task is to process q queries of the form: what is the xor sum of values in range [a, b]?
explanation: Since x ^ x = 0, the XOR sum of range [a, b] is simply prefXor[b] ^ prefXor[a - 1].

title: Exponentiation
statement:
Your task is to efficiently calculate the values a^b modulo 10^9 + 7.
Note that in this task we assume that 0^0 = 1.
explanation: Square-and-multiply binary exponentiation computes a^b mod M in O(log b) multiplications.

title: Counting Divisors
statement:
Given n integers, your task is to report for each integer the number of its divisors.
For example, if x = 18, the correct answer is 6 because its divisors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18.
explanation: Precompute divisor counts for all integers up to MAX = 10^6 using a sieve in O(MAX log MAX) time: for i = 1..MAX, for j = i, 2i, 3i..MAX, divs[j]++.

title: Common Divisors
statement: You are given an array of n positive integers. Your task is to find two integers such that their greatest common divisor is as large as possible.
explanation: Count frequencies freq[v] of all input numbers. Iterate potential GCD g from MAX down to 1, summing freq[g] + freq[2g] + freq[3g] + ... The first g with total multiples >= 2 is the maximum GCD.

title: String Matching
statement: Given a string s and a pattern p, your task is to count the number of positions where the pattern occurs in the string.
explanation: Build the KMP prefix function (pi table) on the concatenated string "p#s". Count how many positions have pi[i] == |p|.

title: Word Combinations
statement: You are given a string of length n and a dictionary containing k words. In how many ways can you create the string using the words?
constraints:
1 <= n <= 5000
1 <= k <= 10^5
total length of words <= 10^6
explanation: Use dynamic programming where dp[i] is the number of ways to form the prefix of length i. To transition efficiently, insert all dictionary words into a Trie, and for each position i, traverse the Trie matching the string starting from i.

title: Finding Borders
statement:
A border of a string is a prefix that is also a suffix of the string but not the whole string. For example, the borders of "abcababcab" are "ab" and "abcab".

Your task is to find all border lengths of a given string.
explanation: Compute the prefix function (pi array) from the KMP algorithm or use polynomial hashing. The values pi[n-1], pi[pi[n-1]-1], etc. give the lengths of the borders.

title: Longest Palindrome
statement: Given a string, your task is to determine the longest palindromic substring of the string. For example, the longest palindrome in "aybabtu" is "bab".
explanation: Use Manacher's algorithm to find the longest palindromic substring in O(N) time.

title: Point Location Test
statement:
There is a line that goes through the points p1=(x1,y1) and p2=(x2,y2). There is also a point p3=(x3,y3).

Your task is to determine whether p3 is located on the left or right side of the line or if it touches the line when we are looking from p1 to p2.
explanation: The cross product of vectors (p2-p1) and (p3-p1) determines the relative position. If cross > 0, left; if cross < 0, right; if cross == 0, touches.

title: Polygon Area
statement:
Your task is to calculate the area of a given polygon. The polygon consists of n vertices (x1,y1), (x2,y2), ..., (xn,yn). The vertices are given in either clockwise or counterclockwise order.

Since the area can be a fraction, print 2 * area, which is always an integer.
explanation: Use the shoelace formula. The area is half the absolute value of the sum of (xi*yi+1 - xi+1*yi).
